newsitem.title: UK: FOREX MOVE SEEN TEMPTING FOREIGNERS INTO ROMANIA.
newsitem.headline: FOREX MOVE SEEN TEMPTING FOREIGNERS INTO ROMANIA.

text.p: Romanian stocks should attract a wider range of foreign investors following long-awaited central bank approval of profit repatriation procedures, London analysts said on Wednesday.
France Cloud of Nomura said the move would open the market to funds which until now had been prevented from investing in Romania due to the difficulties in repatriating profits.
"I think we will see a steady increase in flows. At the moment it is very variable," she said.
Romania's central bank said earlier that non-resident investors would in future be able to buy dollars for lei in the local foreign exchange market, in relation to their local investments.

Analysts said the new procedures, which will be effective once published in the Official Gazette, put flesh on the bones of legislation in June which first gave repatriation a green light in principle.
"We view this as a significant hurdle which has now been removed," said Tim Harris of Societe Generale European Emerging Markets.
"Repatriation is everything. The fact that people couldn't get their money out was a major stumbling-block."
The government previously announced that a tax of up to 1.5 percent would be applied to each portfolio deal.

Romania's small equity market has seen increased international interest this year, supported by growing confidence in the centrist government which won last November's elections, ending seven years of ex-communist rule.
